    "Recent and repeated interactions provide specific clues about the active task, performer, mood, or desired experience that broader historical interests can obscure.",
    "Existing ownership can indicate a satisfied need; complementary additions require a different justification from replacements or duplicates.",
    "Users choose selectively when an item's practical fit or entertainment appeal is identifiable; weakly established relevance does not reliably translate into willingness to choose."

    "The frequency of rejection for redundancy, incompatible specifications, unsupported equipment needs, or assumed projects.",
    "The relative ranks of choices tied to recent, specific interests versus rejected items sharing only a broad category or ecosystem.",
    "The frequency of uncertain judgments caused by insufficient item identification, separated from explicit preference mismatches."
  ]
